pronunciation: Standard academic (modern Israeli-based), as most seminaries teach
note: Hand-written. Example words are vocab.json entries (strongs + key, checked by scripts/build-hebrew-course.js); an optional form is a spelling that occurs in orig/ot as that word. exampleRefs are verse references whose text comes from orig/ot at display time. Sound-alikes are American English. Vowel signs are shown on the letter ב so they can be seen.

transliteration.scheme: STEPBible TAHOT (the t field of orig/ot)
transliteration.summary: One Latin letter or pair per consonant: א and ע ' (an apostrophe), ב b with a dot (dagesh) and v without, ג g, ד d, ה h, ו v, ז z, ח ch, ט t, י y, כ k with a dot and kh without, ל l, מ m, נ n, ס s, פ p with a dot and f without, צ tz, ק k, ר r, שׁ sh, שׂ s, ת t. Vowels a, e, i, o, u, with no marks for long or short; a vocal shewa is written e; a silent shewa is not written. Syllables are separated by dots, and in running text the stressed syllable begins with a capital letter (be.re.Shit). A doubled consonant (dagesh forte) is written once.
transliteration.dataQuirk: Dictionary forms in the lexicon are written in lower case with no stress (e.lo.him), and some leave out the initial apostrophe of א or ע. vocab.json gives the text's own spelling of the dictionary form where it occurs as it stands, else the lexicon's.

consonants.name: alef
consonants.sound: silent: it carries a vowel (a glottal stop at most)

consonants.name: bet
consonants.sound: b with a dot (בּ), v without (ב)
consonants.soundAlike: בּ = b as in boy; ב = v as in vine

consonants.name: he
consonants.sound: h; silent at the end of a word unless it has a dot (mappiq)

consonants.name: vav
consonants.sound: v; also a vowel letter for o (וֹ) and u (וּ)

consonants.name: chet
consonants.soundAlike: ח = ch as in Scottish loch or German Bach

consonants.name: yod
consonants.sound: y; also a vowel letter for i and e

consonants.name: kaf
consonants.sound: k with a dot (כּ), a throaty kh without (כ)
consonants.soundAlike: כּ = k as in king; כ = ch as in Bach

consonants.name: ayin
consonants.sound: silent in this pronunciation: it carries a vowel
consonants.soundAlike: ע = like א, the catch in uh-oh

consonants.name: pe
consonants.sound: p with a dot (פּ), f without (פ)
consonants.soundAlike: פּ = p as in pen; פ = f as in fun

consonants.name: resh
consonants.sound: r (a throaty r is usual today)

consonants.name: shin / sin
consonants.sound: sh with the dot on the right (שׁ), s with the dot on the left (שׂ)
consonants.soundAlike: שׁ = sh as in shoe; שׂ = s as in sun

finalForms.description: Five letters have a different shape at the end of a word: ך ם ן ף ץ (kaf, mem, nun, pe, tsade). They sound the same.

readingDirection.description: Hebrew is read from right to left. The vowels are dots and dashes written under, over or after the letters; a word is read letter, then its vowel, then the next letter.

begadkephat.letters: ב ג ד כ פ ת
begadkephat.description: Six letters (remember them as b-g-d-k-p-t) can take a dot called dagesh lene at the start of a word or after a closed syllable. In this pronunciation it changes the sound of three of them: בּ b / ב v, כּ k / כ kh, פּ p / פ f. In ג, ד and ת it makes no difference to the sound.

dagesh.name: dagesh lene
dagesh.description: The dot in one of the six begadkephat letters at the start of a syllable: it gives the hard sound (בּ b, כּ k, פּ p).

dagesh.name: dagesh forte
dagesh.description: The same dot in almost any letter after a vowel: the letter is doubled (said twice, or held a little longer). The article הַ doubles the next letter this way.

mappiq.description: A dot in a final ה (הּ) shows it is a real consonant h, not a silent vowel letter. It usually means "her" or "its".

vowels.name: qamets
vowels.note: In a few closed, unstressed syllables the same sign is qamets hatuf, a short o.

vowels.name: hireq
vowels.class: short (long when followed by yod: בִי)

shewa.description: Two dots, one above the other, under a letter: either a very short e (vocal shewa) or no vowel at all (silent shewa).

vocal.rule: Vocal at the start of a word, under a doubled letter, and after a long vowel or another shewa: said as a quick e, as in the a of about.

silent.rule: Silent when it closes a syllable after a short vowel, and at the end of a word under ך.

hatephVowels.name: hateph qamets
hatephVowels.noExampleNote: None of the vocabulary words starts with one; it is common under ח and א (for example in אֳנִי, a ship).

hatephNote: The guttural letters א ה ח ע cannot take a vocal shewa, so they take one of these short vowels instead.

furtivePatach.description: A patach under a final ח, ע or הּ is said BEFORE the letter: רוּחַ is ru-ach, not ru-cha.

syllables.description: Every syllable begins with a consonant and has one vowel. An open syllable ends in its vowel (דָּ in דָּבָר); a closed one ends in a consonant (בָר). Most words are stressed on the last syllable; some are stressed on the one before it (מֶלֶךְ is ME-lekh). The transliteration in the course marks the stress with a capital letter.

marks.name: maqqef
marks.description: A short raised hyphen joining two words into one unit for stress; read the first word lightly. The words are still separate words.

marks.name: sof pasuq
marks.description: Two diamonds at the end of every verse: the full stop.

marks.name: cantillation marks
marks.description: The small marks above and below the words (accents for chanting and for phrasing) are on almost every word. Ignore them for now: they are not vowels. One of them often marks the stressed syllable.

marks.name: paragraph letters
marks.description: A פ or ס standing alone after a verse marks the end of a paragraph. It is not a word.
